components.name: Button
components.usage: Use for an immediate action in the current view.
antipatterns: Do not use for navigation; use ButtonLink.

components.name: Select
components.usage: Use for one value chosen out of a known list, such as a sort order or a theme setting.

examples.label: Sort menu
examples.code:
<Select value={sort} onValueChange={setSort}>
  <SelectTrigger aria-label="Sort by">
    <SelectValue placeholder="Choose sort order" />
  </SelectTrigger>
  <SelectContent>
    <SelectItem value="newest">Newest first</SelectItem>
    <SelectItem value="name">Name</SelectItem>
  </SelectContent>
</Select>

antipatterns: Do not use when the list is searchable or long; use MultiSelect or a combobox pattern.
Do not leave the trigger without an accessible name; pass aria-label or a wired label.

components.name: SelectTrigger
components.usage: The button-like field that opens the choose-one menu. Give it an accessible name.
antipatterns: Do not use a SelectTrigger without a SelectValue so the chosen value is shown.

components.name: SelectValue
components.usage: Shows the current value inside the trigger and a placeholder while nothing is chosen.
antipatterns: Do not render placeholder text as a SelectItem; it would become a selectable option.

components.name: SelectContent
components.usage: The panel that holds the options. It animates with the shared motion tokens.
antipatterns: Do not put forms or buttons inside it; keep it to options.

components.name: SelectGroup
components.usage: Groups related options together with a label.
antipatterns: Do not use a label on its own without a group.

components.name: SelectLabel
components.usage: The heading above a group of options.

components.name: SelectItem
components.usage: One option in a choose-one menu.
antipatterns: Do not use an empty string value; it is reserved for the cleared state.

components.name: SelectSeparator
components.usage: A thin line that separates option groups.
antipatterns: Do not add a separator between every option.

components.name: MultiSelect

props.name: className
props.default: flex flex-wrap items-center gap-1.5 py-1.5 pl-3 pr-9

components.usage: Use when several values must be picked from a long list and the list is not known, such as universities, areas or queues.

examples.label: Pick teams
examples.code:
<MultiSelect
  options={teams}
  value={selected}
  onValueChange={setSelected}
  placeholder="Team members"
  searchPlaceholder="Search people"
/>

antipatterns: Do not use for one value out of a short list; use Select.
Do not hardcode visible strings; pass placeholder, searchPlaceholder, emptyMessage and formatOverflow so the project can translate them.
Do not fetch data inside the component; the project owns the options list.

components.name: Checkbox
components.usage: Use to turn one option on or off, or to select rows in a list.
antipatterns: Do not use for a value with three or more meanings; use a choose-one menu.
Do not build a checkbox from a styled div; this is the real form control with the right ARIA.

components.name: Table
components.usage: Use for structured rows of comparable values, such as statistics or admin listings.
antipatterns: Do not use a table for layout or for cards of unrelated content.
Do not put the sorting logic in the component; the project sorts and reports sortDirection.

components.name: TableHead
components.usage: A column header. When sortable it renders a button and sets aria-sort.
antipatterns: Do not make a column sortable without showing which direction is active.

components.name: TableCell
components.usage: One value in a row. Use align end for numbers so they line up.

components.name: TableEmptyState
components.usage: Shown below the header when no rows match, so the header stays visible.
antipatterns: Do not replace the whole table with the empty state; keep the header so context is not lost.

components.name: ToggleGroup
components.usage: Use for two to five mutually exclusive options that should be compared at a glance, such as Off / Preferred / Required.

examples.label: Requirement level
examples.code:
<ToggleGroup type="single" value={mode} onValueChange={setMode} fullWidth aria-label="Requirement">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="off">Off</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="preferred">Preferred</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="required">Required</ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>

antipatterns: Do not use for more than five options; use a choose-one menu.
Do not use type multiple when only one option may be active.
Do not build a segmented control from plain Buttons; use this component.

components.name: ToggleGroupItem
components.usage: One segment in a toggle group.
antipatterns: Do not use a segment for navigation between pages.

components.name: NavMenu
components.usage: The row of top-level links at the top of a page; it scrolls sideways on narrow screens.

examples.label: Top navigation
examples.code:
<NavMenu aria-label="Main">
  <NavItem asChild active={isHome}><Link to="/">Overview</Link></NavItem>
  <NavItem asChild><Link to="/settings">Settings</Link></NavItem>
</NavMenu>

antipatterns: Do not nest actions or menus in it; use DropdownMenu for those.
Do not leave out aria-label; screen readers announce the region.

components.name: NavItem
components.usage: A top-level link. Sets aria-current="page" when active and shows a tinted background.
antipatterns: Do not use a nav item for a button that runs an action; use Button.
Do not signal the current page with a colour alone; the active state also carries aria-current.
